title: The Richest Man in Babylon
author: George S. Clason
short_description: Clason’s Babylonian parables of money — pay yourself first, make money work, and protect capital.
content_text:
PART 1 — KEY LESSONS (OUTLINE)

1. Pay yourself first

  • Save at least a tenth before spending.

2. Put money to work

  • Invest wisely so money multiplies.

3. Protect capital

  • Avoid tips and risks you don’t understand.

4. Own your dwelling

  • Housing equity as ancient wisdom theme.

5. Increase ability

  • Earn more by growing skill and reliability.

PART 2 — THE RICHEST MAN IN BABYLON

A 26-Minute Read Summary

Chapter 1: Parables of money

George Clason’s Richest Man in Babylon teaches personal finance via ancient parables. The charm is simplicity: timeless rules in story form.

Translate gold to modern currency and habits.

Rules beat gurus.

Teach kids with the stories.

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: Use simple timeless money rules — stories make them sticky.

Chapter 2: A part of all you earn is yours to keep

Pay yourself first — save before lifestyle. Ten percent is classic starting point; adjust upward when possible.

Automate transfers.

Name the account Future You.

Raise percentage with raises.

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: Automate paying yourself first before lifestyle spending.

Chapter 3: Make money work

Idle savings underperform; careful investing compounds. Babylon advises seeking informed counsel and understandable ventures.

Learn basics before complexity.

Prefer boring diversified approaches for most people.

Avoid FOMO tips.

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: Invest patiently in what you understand — prefer boring compounding.

Chapter 4: Guard against loss

Capital protection first. Tips from the uninformed destroy gold.

If you can’t explain the downside, don’t buy.

Emergency funds before speculation.

Insurance where appropriate.

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: Protect capital — skip tipsters and unexplained risk.

Chapter 5: Own where you live theme

Making housing advantageous appears as wisdom in the tales — context differs modern markets. Principle: reduce wasteful rent vulnerability when buying is sound.

Run numbers for your city.

Don’t stretch into fragile ownership.

Rent can be wise too.

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: Treat housing decisions with math — ownership isn’t dogma.

Chapter 6: Increase capacity to earn

Skill, reliability, and industry raise income faster than penny-pinching alone.

Invest in skills with ROI.

Seek hard problems at work.

Reputation is capital.

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: Raise earning power via skill and reliability — not only cutting lattes.

Chapter 7: Debt discipline

Ancient counsel warns against crushing obligations. Modern: attack high-interest debt systematically.

List debts; snowball or avalanche.

Stop adding consumer debt.

Celebrate cleared balances.

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: Attack high-interest debt systematically — stop digging.

Chapter 8: Consistency over windfalls

Wealth from steady rules beats lottery mindsets.

Track net worth quarterly.

Ignore get-rich theater.

Slight edge meets Babylon.

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: Prefer steady rules to lottery windfalls.

Chapter 9: Counsel of the wise

Seek advice from those with demonstrated results and aligned incentives.

Avoid tipsters selling tips.

Fee-only advice when needed.

Read primary sources.

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: Take counsel from proven, aligned advisors — not tip-sellers.

Chapter 10: Generosity and legacy

Babylon stories include fair dealing and provision for family. Wealth without character is incomplete.

Automate giving if values include it.

Estate basics.

Teach heirs rules not only riches.

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: Pair wealth rules with character, fair dealing, and teaching heirs.

Chapter 11: Modern translation checklist

Budget, auto-save, emergency fund, debt plan, index-leaning investing, skill plan, housing math, insurance.

Score yourself 0–8.

Raise one score this month.

Review yearly.

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: Score a modern Babylon checklist and raise one item monthly.

Chapter 12: Start tonight

Move first 10% or next debt payment tonight. Open the account. Set the automation.

Read one parable aloud to family.

Put the book near bills.

Begin.

Write one actionable line from this chapter.

Teach one point this week.

Sunday: practiced vs drifted?

Lesson: Tonight: automate saving or a debt payment — begin the rules.

Deep Practice Block 1: The Richest Man in Babylon

Turn The Richest Man in Babylon into a ten-day field curriculum. Day one: underline only sentences that imply action and rewrite them onto your calendar as verbs with specific times and places. Days two through four: execute at low intensity while collecting friction notes — when you stalled, who helped, which stories excused delay, and which environment cues worked.

Days five through seven: raise difficulty about ten percent without sacrificing sleep, ethics, or key relationships. Days eight through ten: teach one core idea to another person in your own words and write a half-page memo to future-you describing what continues for the next month and which warning signs mean you are sliding back into old patterns.

If you stall completely, shrink the key behavior to a two-minute version and rebuild. Optional crew mode: a thirty-minute weekly huddle with one win, one miss, and one ask. Continuity beats binge inspiration. Measure approach days rather than mood alone. Keep the book as shared weekday language with your crew, not decorative shelf proof that you once meant to change.

Revisit earlier chapters when motivation dips. Identity is the average of returns, not a perfect streak fantasy. Change one variable after each cycle so you can see what actually worked. Protect health and relationships while you train ambition, craft, money habits, or mindset — progress that destroys foundations is theater.

Track which chapters change Tuesday behavior versus which only feel profound on Sunday night. Prefer the former. Share practices, not slogans. Begin again without a courtroom in your head whenever you miss a day.

Lesson: Run ten-day action cycles — calendar verbs, slight difficulty raises, teach, memo, and restart small when needed.
